items.title: Dexter + Franz :: Panoramic Highway
items.summary: While Panoramic Highway draws on a wide array of influences spanning geography and time, it's anchored by the sounds of Marin County’s coastline, where Dexter+Franz recorded at the Panoramic House. Throughout the album, field recordings and samples of the ocean and beaches seamlessly weave in and out of the songs. Waves crash, seagulls chirp, and synth textures float through the mix like gusts of salty sea breeze. In these moments, Panoramic Highway becomes an elemental experience, rooted in the soundscapes of nature. The post Dexter + Franz :: Panoramic Highway first appeared on Aquarium Drun

items.title: Felt :: Be Still (The Beach Boys)
items.summary: Toward the tail end of their ten-album run in the eighties, English jangle pop outfit Felt had sights on 1968's understated Beach Boys classic Friends for the band's only known cover. This transformative take on Dennis Wilson's soulful, momentary piano ballad "Be Still" sits comfortably next to Primal Scream's Screamadelica -era cover of another Dennis gem in "Carry Me Home" (keyboardist Martin Duffy would play in both bands). A shimmering beauty reminiscent of every frosty, ethereal component of the brilliance of Felt. The post Felt :: Be Still (The Beach Boys) first appeared on Aquarium Drun

items.title: Steve Gunn :: Sundowner
items.summary: A long neglected album dates to the beginning of Steve Gunn’s career, when it seemed that the guitarist might become a Takoma-style picker rather than the songwriter/improvisational experimenter he has since turned out to be. The playing is agile and folk-blues focused; the singing, when it comes, is similarly traditional and not as polished as Gunn has become. The music earned the approval of no less than Jack Rose, and its reels and rambles and psychedelic drones feel very much of a piece with the master’s work. The post Steve Gunn :: Sundowner first appeared on Aquarium Drunkard .
